units.rhetorical_move: opens against a pervasive belief

original_instantiations: the common view says the information age has arrived
the data are still not fully exploited

units.source_excerpt: Contrary to the pervasive belief, the data are not fully exploited yet.
units.reusable_pattern: Open by setting a correction against a pervasive belief.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not grant the belief.

units.rhetorical_move: says a well-established market is required
units.function: name what the market must do

original_instantiations: data sit under poor isolated management
a market must price, reward, regulate and protect

units.source_excerpt: A well-established market is required that prices sharing and protects information.
units.reusable_pattern: Require a market and list the jobs it must do.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not stop at the diagnosis.

units.rhetorical_move: calls the model sophisticated and generalized
units.function: praise the model with two adjectives

original_instantiations: the analysis rests on one named dataset
the model is called sophisticated and generalized

units.source_excerpt: We propose a sophisticated and generalized model for the price of private information.
units.reusable_pattern: Praise a model with a pair of adjectives.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a third.

units.rhetorical_move: says the relationship is log-likelihood, not linear

original_instantiations: experiments compare groups
the link between records and worth bends rather than staying straight

units.source_excerpt: The relationship between data and value is not linear, but log-likelihood.
units.reusable_pattern: Reject the obvious shape with not, but.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the linear reading standing.

units.rhetorical_move: says agencies should compensate directly

original_instantiations: a breach and its cascade are simulated
agencies should pay individuals directly

units.source_excerpt: We think agencies should compensate individuals directly for data breaches.
units.reusable_pattern: Soften a firm recommendation with we think.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the directly.

units.rhetorical_move: quotes a volume and a forecast
units.function: anchor the trend with two figures

original_instantiations: one year's volume is given
a later year's forecast is set beside it

units.source_excerpt: One stated volume is generated each day, and a far larger figure is forecast for later.
units.reusable_pattern: Pair a present figure with a forecast.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not give only one of them.

units.rhetorical_move: says people are tricked into offering data

original_instantiations: millions hand over data
the reward they get is little

units.source_excerpt: Millions of people are tricked into offering their data in exchange for little reward.
units.reusable_pattern: Call the exchange unfair with tricked and little reward.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the exchange voluntary.

units.rhetorical_move: says the results convince the authors
units.function: let the result change the authors' mind

original_instantiations: the model gives interesting and reasonable results
those results convince the authors that control must be strict

units.source_excerpt: The results are interesting and reasonable, which convinces us that control must be strict.
units.reusable_pattern: Let a result convince the authors instead of asserting the conclusion.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip the result.

units.rhetorical_move: says the assumptions hold in most cases

original_instantiations: the assumptions hold true in most cases
otherwise they are indisputably satisfiable under regulation

units.source_excerpt: Our assumptions hold true in most cases or are indisputably satisfiable under regulation.
units.reusable_pattern: Bound an assumption with in most cases and give the fallback.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the assumptions always hold.

units.rhetorical_move: says one assumption guarantees an universal understanding

original_instantiations: one assumption guarantees a shared reading of value
the article before universal is an

units.source_excerpt: One assumption guarantees that an universal understanding of data value exists.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep an universal as the writer's phrasing.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct an to a when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: calls one factor unnegligible

original_instantiations: data quality changes the value
the factor is called unnegligible

units.source_excerpt: Another unnegligible factor that affects the value is the quality demanded.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep unnegligible as the writer's word.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct it to non-negligible when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: says there is nothing ambiguous

original_instantiations: further factors also affect value
their existence is called nothing ambiguous

units.source_excerpt: There is nothing ambiguous that a variety of additional factors also have impacts.
units.reusable_pattern: Preface a list with there is nothing ambiguous that.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hedge the list.

units.rhetorical_move: says value does not rise linearly

original_instantiations: a published report is quoted
it says value does not increase linearly with amount

units.source_excerpt: Contrary to popular belief, the value does not increase linearly with its amount.
units.reusable_pattern: Use a cited report to overturn a popular belief.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the correction as your own finding.

units.rhetorical_move: prices general information as a mere fraction

original_instantiations: age, gender and location are priced
the price is called a mere fraction per person

units.source_excerpt: General information is worth a mere fraction per person.
units.reusable_pattern: Belittle an ordinary price with a mere.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the mere.

units.rhetorical_move: says milestones prompt the big changes
units.function: contrast the ordinary with the event

original_instantiations: ordinary attributes are cheap
named life events prompt the major changes in value

units.source_excerpt: It is certain milestones in a person's life that prompt major changes in value.
units.reusable_pattern: Contrast cheap ordinary data with named life events.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat every attribute as equal.

units.rhetorical_move: defines the vector as a sum of conditions

original_instantiations: each satisfied condition adds its value vector
the feature vector is their sum

units.source_excerpt: A person's feature vector is the sum of the value vectors of the conditions satisfied.
units.reusable_pattern: Restate a mechanism with in other words.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a step the algorithm lacks.

units.rhetorical_move: says the correlations are the most magnificent

original_instantiations: the matrix is filled from covariances
three pairs are called the most magnificent

units.source_excerpt: The most magnificent correlations exist between three named pairs of categories.
units.reusable_pattern: Rank results with the most magnificent.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not flatten the ranking.

units.rhetorical_move: says decay with time is widely acknowledged

original_instantiations: worth fades as years pass
the fading is called commonly granted

units.source_excerpt: It is widely acknowledged that data value decays with time.
units.reusable_pattern: Support one factor with it is widely acknowledged.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present it as your derivation.

units.rhetorical_move: says most people would have trouble knowing

original_instantiations: large firms build their business on personal data
most people would have trouble knowing who holds it

units.source_excerpt: Most people would have trouble knowing who exactly has access to their data.
units.reusable_pattern: Contrast a firm's knowledge with what most people cannot see.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the reader knows.

units.rhetorical_move: says the algorithms are progressively gaining popularity
units.function: justify a method by its trend

original_instantiations: clustering on social networks is spreading
the cause is the insight large-scale data produce

units.source_excerpt: Such clustering algorithms are progressively gaining popularity.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify a method by saying it is progressively gaining popularity.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the method is standard.

units.rhetorical_move: says the visualization shows the correlations

original_instantiations: the network is clustered into a stated number of subgroups
the picture shows the correlations between people

units.source_excerpt: The visualization of the network shows the correlations between different people.
units.reusable_pattern: Read a figure as showing the correlations.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a number the figure does not give.

units.rhetorical_move: says value is partially related to status

original_instantiations: the vectors of several subgroups are compared
value is only partially related to age and status

units.source_excerpt: It is clear that the value of a person's data is partially related to age and status.
units.reusable_pattern: Hedge a clear result with partially.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the partially.

units.rhetorical_move: treats protection as an special insurance

original_instantiations: protection is priced like insurance
the article before special is an

units.source_excerpt: We treat data protection as an special insurance.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep an special as the writer's phrasing.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct an to a when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: says the loss is roughly seventy-fold

original_instantiations: the trade value is only a few dollars
the cost of a stolen record is roughly seventy-fold higher

units.source_excerpt: The cost of a stolen record is roughly seventy-fold its trade value.
units.reusable_pattern: Magnify a gap with a fold.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the roughly.

units.rhetorical_move: says sharing might be better when risk is low

original_instantiations: protection costs several times the trade value
sharing and profiting might be better if the risk is low

units.source_excerpt: It might be better to share the data and profit if the risk is low.
units.reusable_pattern: End a calculation with it might be better, under a condition.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the condition.

units.rhetorical_move: calls protection an unnecessary cost

original_instantiations: the risk of disclosure is negligible
spending considerably on protection is then an unnecessary cost

units.source_excerpt: If the risk is negligible, spending considerably on protection would be an unnecessary cost.
units.reusable_pattern: Call spending unnecessary once the risk is negligible.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not recommend the spending anyway.

units.rhetorical_move: says privacy should be made a basic right

original_instantiations: value varies by region and by law
the conclusion is that privacy should be a basic human right

units.source_excerpt: We can draw the conclusion that information privacy should be made a basic human right.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a survey of laws with we can draw the conclusion.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present it as one country's rule.

units.rhetorical_move: says the ratio is usually much higher for the old

original_instantiations: the same leak hits two age groups
the ratio for older people is usually much higher

units.source_excerpt: For older people the ratio is usually much higher than for young people.
units.reusable_pattern: Compare generations with usually much higher.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the usually.

units.rhetorical_move: says the loss should not be neglected

original_instantiations: breach costs are shown across industries
the loss is a factor we should not neglect

units.source_excerpt: The loss is a factor that we should not neglect.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the words run together as printed.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not insert the missing space when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: says demand falls and the price follows
units.function: trace the breach to the price

original_instantiations: buyers turn to breached data instead
demand decreases and the price goes lower

units.source_excerpt: Demand will decrease and the price will be lower.
units.reusable_pattern: Carry a breach through to a lower price.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not stop at the breach.

units.rhetorical_move: says the analysis convinces the authors

original_instantiations: the model stays stable under different conditions
the authors are convinced it solves the problem

units.source_excerpt: The model performs stably, by which we are convinced it solves the problem.
units.reusable_pattern: Report a test with by which we are convinced.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim conviction without the test.

units.rhetorical_move: says the metric proofs the model performs well

original_instantiations: the metric stays small across the experiments
this proofs the model performs well

units.source_excerpt: The metric is very small, which proofs the model performs well.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep proofs where the writer means proves.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct proofs to proves when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: says the method is accurate and generalized enough

original_instantiations: three components make up the method
it is accurate and generalized enough for a wide range of domains

units.source_excerpt: The method is accurate and generalized enough to be adopted widely.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim adoption with accurate and generalized enough.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim it works in every domain.

units.rhetorical_move: calls the method out method

original_instantiations: the current approach needs a large dataset
the method is written as out method

units.source_excerpt: One limitation is stated, and the method is written with a letter missing.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the dropped letter.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not restore the letter when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: plans to cater to deep learning
units.function: name the reason for more data

original_instantiations: the dataset will be extended in scale and coverage
the aim is to cater to deep learning

units.source_excerpt: We plan to extend the dataset to cater to the needs of deep learning.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify more data with to cater to.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the plan without its reason.

units.rhetorical_move: uses a four-line memo header

original_instantiations: the header names the recipient as a decision maker
subject and date follow on their own lines

units.source_excerpt: The memo header gives recipient, sender, subject and date on separate lines.
units.reusable_pattern: Head a policy memo with four labeled lines.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the date.

units.rhetorical_move: says there are discrepancies among the three

original_instantiations: private information resembles property and intellectual property
discrepancies remain among the three

units.source_excerpt: The three are similar, yet there are discrepancies among them.
units.reusable_pattern: Grant a likeness and then name the discrepancies.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not collapse the three into one.

units.rhetorical_move: says the data should not be trackable

original_instantiations: protection belongs to individuals and agencies both
the data should not be trackable by government

units.source_excerpt: Based on our model, the data should not be trackable by the government.
units.reusable_pattern: Derive a prohibition from the model with based on our model.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the prohibition as a law.

units.rhetorical_move: calls for a harmonious ecosystem

original_instantiations: four solutions follow
building the ecosystem requires significant commitment from all stakeholders

units.source_excerpt: Building a harmonious ecosystem will require significant commitment from all stakeholders.
units.reusable_pattern: Preface a list of solutions with the commitment it demands.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not shrink all stakeholders to one party.

units.rhetorical_move: numbers sources in brackets

original_instantiations: each source opens with a bracketed number
online sources carry an available link

units.source_excerpt: Sources open with a bracketed number, and online ones carry a link.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the bracketed numbering.
prohibited_generalizations: The citation list belongs to this paper and does not transfer.

units.rhetorical_move: formats the database as a questionnaire

original_instantiations: the value database is printed as questions
each answer carries a dollar value

units.source_excerpt: The appendix prints the value database as a questionnaire.
units.reusable_pattern: Point at the questionnaire instead of reprinting it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reproduce the values in the body.
